Roughly triples the flat-surface error and consumes most of the 50 m SIM-T01 budget on its own. Mitigations: cant the boresights (halves it), or give the filter an onboard terrain model.
Candidate value for GNC-06 (TBD). Small because the star trackers run until 2 km and gyro drift over the remaining ~50 s is tiny. It would degrade badly if the trackers were turned off earlier.

Notes: 0 of 24 cases met SIM-T01 (50 m). The nominal case lands at 21 m, so this is NOT a guidance tuning problem - the altitude-priority profile law has no position feedback at all, so an injection velocity error integrates essentially unattenuated into landing miss over the 222 s burn. See TR-SIM-23.

Against 380 kg loaded (SIM-M03 minus SIM-M01). 11 of 24 cases ran the tanks DRY before touchdown. The nominal uses 368 kg, i.e. 97% of the load, so there is effectively NO propellant margin for dispersion. A separate finding from the accuracy one and arguably more urgent.

Parameter: MC criterion failure ranking, nominal dispersions
Notes: Landing accuracy is the binding requirement by a wide margin, and descent rate second - both driven by the same cause, cases that run out of propellant and then fall. Attitude and body rate are comfortable, i.e. the attitude control stack is not the problem.

Parameter: Behaviour-cloning run-to-run variance in soft-landing rate
Notes: TWO RUNS WITH IDENTICAL dynamics, expert and loss differed by 25 points (31.7% vs 57.0% soft, final BC mse 0.0389 vs 0.0345). The cause is the DAgger feedback loop: training rolls forward on a mix of expert and policy actions, so a slightly better early policy visits better states, which makes training easier, which makes it better still. CONSEQUENCE: a single BC run is NOT a usable baseline, and any claimed BC or BC+PPO improvement needs several seeds before it means anything. The reward-shaping change made between the two runs cannot explain it - behaviour cloning is supervised regression and ignores the reward entirely.
